question: If A and C interchange their places, B and D interchange their places, E and G interchange their places and so on for rest of the letters in the alphabet, then which letter will be 5th to the left of O?
solution:
According to the question A and C interchange their places, B and D interchange their places, E and G interchange their places, and so on for rest of the letters in the alphabet:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/db8b642f35d5c7d5b47dcdee50bb4c57d0808d4849548a6da271e6b9beb41139.png] 

Thus, according to the final arrangement F is the 5th to the left of O.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**The logic followed here is:

A and C interchange their places → C(3) - 2 = A(1)

B and D interchange their places → D(4) - 2 = B(2)

E and G interchange their places → G(7) - 2 = E(5)

Similarly,

O(15) - 2 = M(13) (Here, O interchange position with M as per the given logic)

so, O's position will be 13th in the series after arrangement

Now, 5th to the left of O in English alphabetic series:

O(13) - 5 = H(8)

And, according to the logic given H interchanged with:

H(8) - 2 = **F(6)**
